page: Vultr vhf-8c-32gb is a High Frequency Compute server configured with an Intel x86_64 processor featuring 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz and utilizes a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 512 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The processor architecture supports Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), AES cryptography, and Bit Manipulation Instruction Set 2 (BMI2), though it lacks AVX-512 and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) capabilities.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics placing in the top 25% and single-threaded gzip compression reaching top-tier status in the top 10%. Memory performance is polarized; while the PassMark memory score ranks in the top 10% and small-block cached read bandwidth is average, large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidths fall into the bottom 25%. Multi-core execution, including Geekbench multi-core compiling and ray tracing, remains in the average tier. Large-model LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with the medium 7B model performing in the bottom 10%, though small 135M model inference remains average.

From a resource density perspective, the combination of 32.0 GB RAM and 512 GB NVMe SSD on a shared CPU architecture offers a balanced hardware profile for general-purpose workloads. The shared CPU allocation introduces potential resource contention, making it less suitable for sustained maximum CPU utilization but highly cost-efficient for bursty workloads. This server is well-suited for static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and lightweight text or image processing tasks that benefit from fast local NVMe storage and strong single-threaded performance.
description: Vultr vhf-8c-32gb is a High Frequency Compute server featuring an Intel x86_64 processor with 8 shared vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 32.0 GB of RAM. It includes 512 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one public IPv4 address. Benchmarks show strong single-core CPU performance and top-tier single-threaded gzip compression, though large-block uncached memory bandwidth and medium-model LLM inference are weak. The shared CPU allocation makes it a cost-efficient option for workloads with variable resource demands. The hardware supports AVX and AES cryptography but lacks AVX-512. Multi-core performance and database operations fall into average tiers, making this instance a balanced choice for non-sustained compute tasks. It is best suited for static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and general-purpose applications.
